LMP3.title: Boyd’s United Ligier wins a class of penalties and breakdowns
LMP3.dek: Boyd, Gamble and Wheldon won from pole by about a minute over Nielsen’s Duqueine as penalties and failures thinned the field, with Eurointernational inheriting third.

facts.v: The mandatory fuel-only stops brought in at Paul Ricard were kept at Spa because the higher consumption of the new Nismo VK56 engines had not been solved.
Boyd’s 2:12.634 put the United Ligier almost nine tenths clear of the field.
RealTeam’s Ligier #8 was third with about 20 minutes left when a failure at Turn 1 ended its race, promoting Eurointernational.
DKR Engineering was fined 250 euros after Glorieux took the chequered flag twice at the end of the 4 Hours of Spa.

chapters.title: The fuel problem carries over
text: LMP3 reached Spa with its fuel issue unsolved. The extra timed fuel-only stops introduced at Paul Ricard, after ORECA found the new Nismo VK56 engines used more fuel than predicted, were kept for this weekend through an amended bulletin. Nielsen had used up the hours on its older VK50 engines at the opener and switched to newer units.

The rear wings of all Duqueine D08 cars had been returned to the factory for checks after the wing failure on Wells’s car at Paul Ricard. Eurointernational added Laskaratos to the #11 after Kari was upgraded from Silver to Gold, RLR MSport signed Megennis for the #15, and RealTeam’s Ligier was back on track after trouble in Wednesday testing.

chapters.title: Boyd almost nine tenths clear
text: Boyd set pole on 2:12.634 in the #2 United Ligier he shares with Gamble and Wheldon, 0.885 seconds quicker than anyone. Hörr was second in DKR’s Duqueine #4 and Droux third for Realteam’s Ligier. Tappy’s United #3, Jakobsen’s RLR #15 and Kari’s Eurointernational #11 were next, all more than a second and a half off the pace; the #11 had stopped briefly on its out lap.

chapters.title: Hippe in the barrier
text: The first safety car came in the opening hour. Hodes spun the Nielsen Duqueine #10 at Speakers Corner, and Hippe crashed Inter Europol’s Ligier #13 into the tyre barrier and was out. Hodes drove away, and Nielsen replaced the rear floor, legality panels and right rear suspension to send the car back out.

chapters.title: A race of attrition
text: The #2 was largely unchallenged, with Wells and Noble’s Nielsen Duqueine #7 the only car keeping it honest. Behind them the order was rewritten by penalties and failures. RLR’s #15 lost time to a nightmare stint from Dayson and to penalties that took it from a podium place to seventh. BHK’s #16 troubled Race Control repeatedly. DKR’s #4 collected a pair of penalties, United’s #3 pitted early for a replacement steering wheel and Graff’s #9 had penalties and off-track moments. The repaired #10 stopped late with a mechanical failure.

chapters.title: RealTeam lose third at Turn 1
text: RealTeam’s #8 had run through multiple excursions and more than one penalty but still sat third with 20 minutes left. A failure at Turn 1 stopped it, and Eurointernational’s Ligier #11 of Erdos, Kari and Laskaratos took third.

chapters.title: United’s double and a 250-euro fine
text: The #2 won on 95 laps, about a minute ahead of Nielsen’s #7 on the same lap. The #11 was third on 93, then Graff’s Ligier #9, United’s #3, DKR’s #4, RLR’s #15 (seventh), Graff’s Duqueine #5 and BHK’s #16 (ninth). Wheldon set the class fastest lap, 2:16.667. The #8, #10 and #13 were not classified.

United took LMP3 as well as LMP2 again, having claimed both prototype poles. DKR was fined 250 euros after Glorieux took the chequered flag twice at the end of the race. The series next went back to Paul Ricard for a second round.

LMGTE.title: Kessel wins as Proton’s leading Porsche is undone by a puncture at Raidillon
LMGTE.dek: Perel, Broniszewski and Gomes won for Kessel Racing after Proton’s #77 Porsche, which had led, suffered a puncture and spin at Raidillon; AF Corse’s guesting Ferrari took second.

facts.v: A 12-car class, including four guesting WEC cars, was the largest in the ELMS since the Estoril finale of 2014.
Lietz put the Proton Porsche #93 on pole, with Perel’s Kessel Ferrari second two tenths behind.
Proton’s #77 Porsche led until Beretta spun at Raidillon, which handed first place to Kessel.
Red River Sport’s #62 Ferrari withdrew after the UK imposed quarantine on travellers from Belgium.

chapters.title: The biggest GTE field since 2014
text: Twelve GTE cars entered, including four guesting FIA WEC cars, the largest class field in the ELMS since the Estoril finale of 2014. Aston Martin Racing returned for its second and last planned ELMS start with Farfus making his debut for the team. AF Corse’s customer Ferrari ran as the renumbered #88.

The #54 AF Corse Ferrari was badly damaged when Flöhr went off at the Esses in testing, and a replacement car was built up by Thursday morning. Red River Sport’s #62 Ferrari withdrew after the UK imposed quarantine on travellers from Belgium. JMW’s #66 Ferrari arrived with blue additions to its yellow livery and its intended line-up of Hutchison, Jeannette and Sales.

chapters.title: Lietz on pole without ballast
text: Lietz took pole for Proton Competition in the #93 Porsche on 2:17.778, with Fassbender due to start. The car carried no success ballast after Proton’s misfortune at Paul Ricard, and the team used two sets of new Goodyears. Farfus briefly topped the times on his Aston Martin debut before track limits deleted his lap, and he recovered only to fourth.

Perel was second, two tenths behind, in Kessel’s #74 Ferrari, whose attack was blunted when the car needed a replacement rear wing and could not rejoin in time. Piccini was third in the Iron Lynx #60.

chapters.title: Dalla Lana leads, then the Iron Lynx hits the wall
text: Dalla Lana’s opening stint put the Aston Martin #98 into the lead early. Ried took second for Proton’s #77 after a wheel-to-wheel fight with Broniszewski’s Kessel Ferrari, with Perrodo’s #88 and Fassbender’s #93 close behind. Contact in the early running between JMW’s #66 and Iron Lynx’s #83 cost JMW six laps. Shortly before the end of the hour, Schiavoni’s Iron Lynx #60 hit the wall after being tapped by United’s LMP2 Oreca #32, which brought out a safety car.

chapters.title: Raidillon decides it
text: Proton’s #77 took the lead and, through Picariello and Beretta, looked on course for the win until Beretta spun at Raidillon with a left-rear puncture and limped most of a lap back to the pits. That left Perel in front for Kessel, and his pace kept the chasers out of reach. The #54 AF Corse Ferrari stopped mid-race, bringing out another safety car. Spirit of Race’s #55 fought back from an early hit on Cameron but was off strategy, and the #98 fell down the order after a strategy call went awry.

chapters.title: Aston Martin hold off the Proton Porsche
text: Perel brought the #74 home for the win. Behind came Perrodo, Collard and Newey in the #88 AF Corse Ferrari. The Aston Martin #98, which Farfus had pushed hard to return to the podium, finished third, fending off Proton’s #93 at the end.

chapters.title: Kessel’s win and a heavy toll
text: The #74 won on 94 laps, with the #88 on the same lap, the #98 third on 93, then Proton’s #93, Spirit of Race’s #55, the #77 in sixth and AF Corse’s #51 seventh. The all-female Iron Lynx #83, which collected a late penalty, was eighth and JMW’s #66 ninth. The #54 and #60 were not classified. Laser set the class fastest lap, 2:19.467.

Kessel took the win after a weekend in which a run to the front in the Michelin Le Mans Cup had been taken away by a post-race penalty. AF Corse and Proton began reconfiguring their garages for the WEC round at the same circuit the following weekend, and the ELMS next returned to Paul Ricard.
